exposure: cerclage plus vaginal progesterone postoperatively (dual therapy)
outcome: pregnancy latency period from cerclage to delivery
cohort: The study included 122 patients with singleton pregnancies, without prior spontaneous preterm birth, who had cerclage placement before 24 weeks' gestation due to cervical length <10 mm or cervical dilation.
finding: Dual therapy was associated with a lower risk of delivery at <28 weeks' gestation in crude analysis, a longer pregnancy latency from cerclage to delivery (16.3 vs. 14.4 weeks), and greater gestational age at delivery (37.3 vs. 35.8 weeks' gestation) compared with monotherapy.
gest_age: Mean gestational age at delivery was 37.3 weeks for the dual therapy group and 35.8 weeks for the monotherapy group.
